ai_summary: Great Britain’s wind generation currently stands at 2.8 GW, with Scotland delivering an estimated 1.9 GW, which accounts for 18.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This clean generation enables Scotland to achieve an optimal carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the broader GB-wide carbon intensity of 183 gCO2/kWh. However, grid transmission bottlenecks prevent the full transfer of this zero-carbon electricity across the wider network. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 490 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £30,168. To replace this curtailed renewable volume, conventional generation elsewhere had to step in, burning an estimated 93,100 m3 of gas and releasing an additional 172 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s constraint spend indicates an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of £11 million. While calculating the exact invoice impact across Great Britain strictly requires total national demand figures not provided in the operational metrics, distributing an annualized £11 million constraint cost across the wider British system equates to an estimated invoice increase of well under £0.10/MWh, reinforcing the ongoing financial and carbon costs of transmission limits.
